one_line_reason: Small but clean single-ingredient human trials show oral Uncaria tomentosa/guianensis (cat's claw) extract benefits immune response to vaccination, osteoarthritis knee pain, and cancer-related quality of life.

selected.intervention: C-Med-100, a water-soluble extract of Uncaria tomentosa (cat's claw), oral, 2 months
selected.primary_outcome: immune response to 23-valent pneumococcal vaccine (antibody titers, lymphocyte/neutrophil ratio)
selected.why_selected: clean single-ingredient trial with a clear dose showing statistically significant immune enhancement and no toxic side effects.

selected.population: adults with osteoarthritis of the knee (n=45: 30 treated, 15 placebo)
selected.intervention: freeze-dried cat's claw (Uncaria guianensis), oral, 4 weeks
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (freeze-dried preparation, specific mg dose not given)
selected.why_selected: positive RCT with benefits appearing within the first week and no adverse effects on blood/liver function versus placebo, though it uses a different (though related) Uncaria species.

selected.population: patients with advanced solid tumors and no further therapeutic options (n=51, prospective phase II)
selected.intervention: Uncaria tomentosa (cat's claw) dry extract, oral, three times daily
selected.primary_outcome: quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), fatigue, anxiety/depression, sleep quality
selected.why_selected: clear single-ingredient dose in a different (palliative oncology) population, showing improved quality of life and reduced fatigue, though without a placebo comparator.

blockers: The osteoarthritis trial (11603848) uses Uncaria guianensis, a related but different species from the Uncaria tomentosa used in the immune-response and cancer trials, and from what most catalog cat's claw products likely list; species substitution is a real pharmacological uncertainty.
The cancer quality-of-life study (25495394) is an open-label, uncontrolled (no placebo arm described) phase II study in a terminal-cancer population, not general supplement users.
Cat's claw significantly increases blood levels of antiretroviral drugs (per handoff record 27655839), an interaction risk relevant to any general-population use drawn from these trials.

handoff_pmids.note: Systematic review of dietary supplement-antiretroviral interactions; found cat's claw significantly increases levels of certain antiretroviral drugs, recommending patient monitoring for adverse effects.

excluded_pmids.reason: Meta-analysis of preclinical (animal, in vivo) studies on Uncaria tomentosa's anti-inflammatory activity; not human evidence.

Broad Cochrane review of many systemic therapies (pharmacological, dietary supplements, CAM) for aromatase-inhibitor-induced musculoskeletal symptoms in breast cancer; the abstract gives no cat's-claw-specific finding.
RCT of a topical 2% Uncaria tomentosa gel for denture stomatitis; a topical/local application to the palate and denture, not a swallowed oral supplement.
RCT of CognoBlend, a 5-herb combination formula (Bacopa, Ginkgo, Cat's Claw, Gotu Kola, Rosemary) for hepatic encephalopathy; effect cannot be isolated to cat's claw alone.
